page.title: Best Wireless Gaming Headset with Swappable Battery (2026)
page.h1: Best wireless gaming headset with a swappable battery
page.desc: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni, Glorious InfinitePlay and Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II compared on hours per pack, what happens during a swap, platforms and price.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best wireless gaming headset with swappable battery is the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni ({buy:steelseries-arctis-nova-pro-omni}): two batteries rated up to 30 hours each (SoundGuys measured 32 hours 51 minutes on one), and one base that mixes up to 4 sources at once (2 USB, Bluetooth and line-in) across PC, PlayStation, Xbox and Switch. The sound does stop while you swap: put the charged spare in within 8 seconds and the headset powers back on by itself.

If you want the sound to keep playing through a swap, or want to pay less, the Glorious GHS Wireless InfinitePlay is the better pick. A small internal battery keeps it running while you change packs, and each pack is rated 85 hours. It was $199.99 at Glorious on 2026-11-14 but out of stock there that day. It has no active noise cancelling, and Glorious does not list Xbox support. The Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II ($349.99 at Turtle Beach on 2026-11-14) is rated 40 hours per pack. You have to choose its Xbox or PC/PlayStation version, and it weighs 13.9 oz against the Omni's 12.0 oz.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Heat, clamp and ear cup size (9 mentions). Owners say the leatherette pads get hot after an hour or two and the cups feel small. One long-term Nova Pro Wireless owner replaced the pads and says the headband lost tension. SoundGuys found the Omni's cups warm after about an hour.
  • Dropouts (5). Best Buy and Slickdeals buyers report lost connections on the Nova Pro Wireless. Some say a firmware update fixed it.
  • Sound stops during the swap (4). This is true on SteelSeries headsets. The headset powers off and comes back on by itself if the spare goes in within 8 seconds. Of these headsets, only the Glorious is confirmed to keep playing.
  • Base screen stays lit (4). Nova Pro Wireless owners say the base display can't be turned off and glows in a dark room. SoundGuys flags a burn-in risk on the Omni's screen.
  • Price (4) and mic (3). SoundGuys calls the Omni mic slightly muffled. Teammates in Notebookcheck's test heard it as clear.

Which one by need

  • PC plus a console, with Discord in your ear: Arctis Nova Pro Omni ({buy:steelseries-arctis-nova-pro-omni}). One model works with PC, PlayStation, Xbox and Switch, and it mixes 4 sources at once.
  • Sound that never stops, or the lowest price: Glorious GHS Wireless InfinitePlay. It is rated 85 hours per pack and runs on an internal reserve during a swap. It has no ANC and no Xbox support listed, and it was out of stock at Glorious on 2026-11-14.
  • Longest pack with ANC on one console: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II, rated 40 hours per pack. Buy the version that matches your console. It is the heaviest here at 13.9 oz.

Not recommended

Arctis Nova Pro Wireless ({buy:steelseries-arctis-nova-pro-wireless-pc-ps}) near list price. It gets 22 hours per pack, plays one base source at a time and comes in separate Xbox and PC/PlayStation versions. It was on backorder on 2026-11-14. Buy it only on a deep sale; otherwise the Omni is worth the extra cost. Arctis Nova Elite ($599.99, backordered on 2026-11-14): Notebookcheck says the Omni brings its main upgrades for $200 less.

notes: Query choice: today's results for 'best wireless gaming headset with swappable battery' are thin: spammy roundups (mayfairfarms, thewearify, foliumbiosciences, narcosis-the-game, lynnbarsigianphotography), product pages and single reviews, with no researched comparison. I could not check autocomplete directly. SteelSeries' store is not Shopify (storecheck returned 404), and plain WebFetch shows no prices because they load by JavaScript, so I read prices through the r.jina.ai reader on 2026-11-14. Prices: Omni $399.99 (White in stock, delivery Nov 17-21; Black on backorder, restock est. Nov 18); Nova Pro Wireless White PC|PS $293.96 vs $299.99 MSRP (backorder); Nova Elite $599.99 (backorder). Rivals: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II $349.99 (Add to Cart, 40 h per pack, 393 g, separate Xbox and PC/PS versions); Glorious InfinitePlay $199.99 sale / $229.99 regular, out of stock, 85 h per pack, 360 g, no Xbox listed, 2-year warranty. Pain-point counts across Slickdeals (9 commenters), Best Buy and Staples snippets, Club386, SoundGuys, Notebookcheck and T3: heat/comfort/cup size 9, dropouts 5, sound stops during swap 4, base screen always on or burn-in 4, price 4, mic 3, one source at a time on Nova Pro Wireless 2, battery not charging 2, packs hard to grip 1. Winners by segment: PC plus a console with mixed audio -> Omni (one model for all platforms, 4-source mix, ANC, 339 g); never-stop or budget -> Glorious InfinitePlay (no program, plain maker link); longest pack with ANC on one platform -> Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II (no program). The swap answer comes from SteelSeries support: the headset powers back on by itself if the swap takes 8 seconds or less, and SoundGuys and Notebookcheck confirm it powers off. UNVERIFIED, kept off the page or labeled: the 30 h per-pack rating comes from Notebookcheck ('up to 60 hours with both batteries, ANC off') and retailer listings, not the SteelSeries page, which shows no hours; the US warranty term (no warranty page found); Midnight Blue Omni availability; the Black PC/PS Nova Pro Wireless price; PC Gamer's 15-20 h per pack with ANC plus Bluetooth (search snippet only); Stealth Pro II swap behavior (TechRadar and PC Gamer disagree); Glorious reserve length (about 3 h, quoted from PC Gamer on Glorious' blog). PRICE FLAG: Notebookcheck's Amazon widget showed the Omni at $317.40 on 2026-11-14, which would be well under SteelSeries' $399.99. amzcheck returned nothing (walled), so this is unverified and not on the page. When amzcheck answers again, recheck: if Amazon is cheaper, the Omni's lead link should go to Amazon. OMNI50 was read on steelseries.com/deals and banners; it ends 2026-11-15 and has not been cart-tested. I could not read Tom's Hardware, PC Gamer, TechRadar, Windows Central, Tom's Guide or GamesRadar (truncated or 403), so no facts from them are used except as noted.
